title: A retrospective study evaluated MedJev for in-hospital mortality prediction
summary: Using records available 24 hours after admission, MedJev ranked eventual in-hospital deaths with an AUROC of 0.926 (95% confidence interval 0.881 to 0.960). The supervised XGBoost comparison scored 0.902, with a paired interval that included no difference. MedJev’s unadjusted risk estimates were substantially miscalibrated.
ai_technology: MedJev, based on Qwen3.5-9B; Platt scaling

source_review.scope: §§3.1–3.4 and 4.2–4.3, Tables 1 and 3–4 and front matter

evidence.tested: Adult patients still hospitalized at 24 hours were eligible. Evaluation examples and supervised-model/recalibration fitting used the source-described patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV MEDS partitions. Recalibration used separately partitioned labeled records and improved calibration without changing AUROC.
evidence.unknown: The retrospective single-center data do not establish external performance or patient benefit. MedJev was first adapted on MIMIC-IV Note, but the primary Methods do not explicitly establish that this adaptation excluded the evaluated patients or their later notes. The described MEDS evaluation split therefore does not authenticate checkpoint-level patient independence or absence of note-derived outcome exposure. The discrimination comparison was against supervised models at the tested local-label budget, not unlimited supervised training.
evidence.ai_role: MedJev converted patient-history events available at the prediction time into outcome-token probabilities, which were evaluated against recorded deaths.
